Types of HDD Enclosures

Single Drive Enclosures The most common option. Fits 1 HDD or SSD and connects using USB. Perfect for private data backups, file transfers or storage expansion for your laptop.

Multi-Bay Enclosures Two or more drives. Ideal for home media servers, NAS installations or large business environments requiring a great deal of storage space in one device.

Portable Enclosures Slim & Light. Usually bus powered, that is no separate power adapter required, and for 2.5" drives. Ideal for those on the move or on the job.

Desktop Storage Enclosures Bigger sizes for 3.5" drives. Requires an external power supply. Better suited for home or office use where high capacity is the priority.

HDD and SSD Compatible Enclosures Many enclosures are able to hold both traditional HDDs and solid state drives. A compatible component will be able to be upgraded or swapped out without purchasing a new enclosure.

  • Drive size: Ensure your drive is 2.5" or 3.5", since cases vary.
  • Connection type: Common types are USB 3.0 and USB-C.

Storage capacity needs: Most users can use single-drive cases. Multi-bay solutions are appropriate for users who require more or redundant storage.

Portability: If you must take your drive on a regular basis, then opt for a thin-bus powered enclosure.

Home vs. business use: If it is used at home, then it might only require one enclosure. For businesses, multi-bay is required or multiple units needed for team access.

Future needs: Make sure it is an enclosure that will accommodate your future storage requirements or speedier connection, if needed, so you don't end up replacing it later.
